evidence.fact: Commercial AI skin-analysis tools already scan a face from a photo, detect about 15 skin concerns such as redness, wrinkles and texture, and then generate a personalised product routine with explanations.

Consumer AI skincare apps recommend products based on skin type and explain which ingredient targets which concern, although they state their advice is informational only. The salon version of this task still depends on in-person skin assessment, demonstrating how to apply products and building client trust during the service.

State cosmetology boards regulate skin-care services, meaning the physical treatments, under the license. Makeup demonstrations and product advice are not described as acts only a licensee may perform, so no human sign-off is required to recommend products.
One vendor's AI agent connects to Booqable rental software. It reads live inventory to check availability and can create bookings and look up customers. Staff still handle the physical logistics.
Rently's AI agent on WhatsApp answers questions about availability, pricing and requirements, and records reservations in the rental system. Complex requests and VIP customers go to human staff.
Bookyt's rental chatbot matches a customer's question to the rental offering, asks for any missing details, and points to booking. This covers much of the discussion about type, quality and quantity.
Conversational-commerce AI agents already greet online shoppers proactively, answer questions and recommend products to identify needs. Fin puts the 2026 market at about $10–14B.
Gorgias says proactive AI engagement drove 50% of conversation-driven purchases during BFCM 2025, which shows AI handling the greet-and-qualify step in digital channels. This is vendor data.

Agentic commerce tools such as Salesforce Agentforce Commerce work in digital storefronts. On the shop floor, greeting and reading customers face to face needs physical presence, which a bodiless agent lacks, so its role there is limited to helping staff (product lookup, suggestions).

Microsoft Brand Agents bring the advice a store associate would give into a chat on the retailer's website, including guidance, upselling and cross-selling. Google, OpenAI, Shopify and PayPal are building similar conversational shopping where customers compare and buy in one place.

In stores, AI copilots and voice-headset assistants support human associates by giving them product, inventory and recommendation data in real time. The associate still serves the customer face to face and physically finds the items.

Manhattan Active Omni's Store Associate Agent answers natural-language questions about inventory and customer behavior, so an agent can handle the 'locate or obtain' step through software. Gaps in universal carts, APIs and product data still limit full deployment.

AI travel chatbots and agents already put together information tailored to the traveler's itinerary and nationality. This includes visa and entry rules, transit requirements, local customs and etiquette, so the main step of assembling the information is automated.

No-code AI agents automatically check visa and entry eligibility by nationality and destination and alert users when requirements change. Guidance for travel agents still advises checking AI drafts against official sources.

IATA Timatic gives travel agents passport, visa and health requirements for over 220 countries, online or by API. That makes the authoritative regulation data digitally reachable, so an agent can send it to the customer by email or in a document instead of handing over a printed brochure.

Vendor pages describe AI agents that run program enrollment from start to finish. They ask qualifying questions, send eligible applicants on to enrollment, offer waitlists or other programs to the rest, and follow up automatically by email or SMS. These are marketing claims and have not been independently checked.

The same vendor offers agents for government health-program enrollment. They pre-screen applicants on household income, family size and participation in other programs, and they collect registration details.

A guide on automating financial aid recommends that AI handle screening, flagging, document requests and status outreach, while humans make the final eligibility or award decisions. Low-confidence cases should go to a human, and every automated decision should be logged.

AI tools such as S7 PLC Buddy, which uses Claude, can read live PLC diagnostics over the network and suggest likely causes. The vendor notes that the operational data agents need is spread across separate systems like SCADA, historians and fleet software.
Agent products for field technicians combine live readings, error logs and maintenance history to help with troubleshooting, but a technician still does the hands-on work.

Under NFPA 70E, touching energized parts with probes or test equipment counts as energized work. It must be done by a qualified person physically present with the right PPE, so diagnosing with meters and scopes needs someone on site.

Vendor pages say hotel revenue-management systems (RoomPriceGenie, PricingService.ai, RoomRaccoon/Pricepoint) set room rates on their own from competitor prices, booking pace and occupancy, push them to the PMS and channel manager, and offer an autopilot mode. These are vendor claims, not independent results.

Hotel budgeting tools such as Otelier TruePlan pull actuals from PMS, POS and accounting systems and use pre-built drivers to cut budget build time. Building the budget still needs input from department heads, and the owner or GM must approve how funds are split between departments.
Vendor buyer's guides say AI budgeting and forecasting software automates driver-based forecasts and budget updates. I found no evidence of fully autonomous budget approval or fund allocation.

Code for America and Anthropic built a SNAP Policy Navigator that answers policy questions with cited sources, but the eligibility decision stays with humans. This shows AI can handle the research and interpretation steps of eligibility policy work.

Research on Rules as Code found that LLMs are useful for summarizing and interpreting SNAP and Medicaid policy but not ideal for implementing strict formulas such as benefit calculations, so humans still need to review the work.
Human service agency standards give policy-setting responsibility to the volunteer board, so deciding policy and being accountable for it stays with people.
O*NET lists 'confer with customer representatives to review schematics and answer questions pertaining to installation of systems' as a task of Mechanical Drafters (17-3013.00).

AI tools in 2026 index CAD files, PDFs and scanned drawings and return source-cited answers to technical questions. This automates retrieval and drafting of answers, but vendors describe these as tools for internal engineering teams, not as agents that hold customer meetings on their own.

Electrical CAD software (WSCAD ELECTRIX AI 2026) has built-in assistants that answer technical installation questions such as wire sizing. This supports partial automation of answering questions about schematics.

State environmental agencies increasingly run permitting and public notices through electronic systems. Louisiana's 2026 SB 99 gives emailed and electronic notices the same legal weight as mailed ones. An agent can handle these digital channels.

RCRA permit and closure documents have to be placed in publicly accessible locations near the facility or at agency offices, and notices go out to facility mailing lists. Some distribution is still on paper or in person.
Some state programs, such as Maryland's, still ask for hard copies and use mail alongside email. This leaves physical sub-steps for a human, or for a print-and-mail service.

Integrated library systems already handle circulation, patron, inventory and serials records and produce reports in software, so an agent with access to the ILS could compile and update these records through the software itself.
Automated circulation modules keep transaction records, overdue notices, item status (lost, missing, withdrawn), stock verification and report generation, so much of the record-keeping is digital.

Physical stock-taking and equipment checks are still done with handheld RFID readers or shelf scanning. That is the physical input a human (or robot) has to supply before the records can be checked against what is on the shelves.

AI agents bought a Czech ad campaign from start to finish, linking Omnicom Media and publisher MAFRA through an MCP gateway and the Ad Context Protocol (AdCP). This is the vendor's own account and has not been independently checked.

At Cannes 2026, Yahoo DSP's Agent Network, TikTok's Symphony Agent and others launched agents that buy and sell ads. A PubMatic executive warned that reliability problems would be common in agent-run media buying.
AdCP was launched in October 2025 with a Media Buy protocol built on MCP. In the first live agent-run media buy, a human approved the purchase.

Manufacturer services such as Sysmex BeyondCare and Ortho's Remote Monitoring Center already do remote calibration, QC monitoring and predictive alerts. Software can therefore take over the data side (QC trend review, scheduling, alerting), but a human still loads calibrators and reagents and does the hands-on maintenance on site.

A clinical-analyzer QC patent describes analyzers sending calibration and QC data and alarms over a network to manufacturer service servers for statistical analysis. This means only some data and diagnostic sub-steps can be done remotely.

CLIA 42 CFR 493.1255 requires labs to perform and document calibration verification at least every 6 months and after major preventive maintenance. CMS surveys cite labs that miss this, so qualified lab personnel remain accountable.

Pharmacy software such as Cegedim Pharmacy Manager's 'Fast Labelling' already fills in the patient, product, directions and quantity from an electronic prescription, so most label preparation is software-driven typing and printing. An agent using the computer could do the remaining data entry and trigger the print.

In pharmacy automation such as Parata Max, integrated printers already produce labels with patient details, medication, dosage instructions, barcodes and regulatory data without anyone typing them. Someone still has to handle the printed label and attach it to the container.

State rules (for example Arizona R4-23-1104 and Mississippi Art. XL) let technicians type and print labels but require a pharmacist to verify their accuracy and hold that pharmacist responsible for the data entered. A human review step therefore stays in place.

Kitchen display systems already pace items by cook time so they reach the expo window together. For example, a 20-minute steak is fired before a 12-minute salmon, and shorter-cook items are held back. This automates the scheduling part of the task.

Toast POS has a 'fire by prep time' item-pacing setting that sends items to stations based on their cook times. It relies on configured cook times, not on what is actually happening at the grill, so the cook still adjusts in real time.
KDS vendors offer course pacing, fire timing and course-hold functions with set gaps between courses, which shows the sequencing logic can be done in software.

Vendors say their bar ID-scanning software runs more than 75 automated checks on each ID and flags suspicious documents. They claim it detects up to 95% of fake IDs when paired with UV/IR/hologram hardware. These are vendor claims with no independent testing found.

Some systems combine document scanning with AI facial age estimation (Yoti) to catch good fakes. Software can do the authenticity and age-calculation steps, but someone still has to take the physical card and match the face to the photo at the bar.

States such as California require ID checkers to complete Responsible Beverage Service training. Their 'diligent inspection' defense, and North Carolina's point-of-sale carding with server liability, put legal responsibility on a human server.

By 2026, voice AI agents (SoundHound at Red Lobster and Five Guys, plus Aldelo's POS voice agent) take restaurant phone and drive-thru orders end to end and send them to the POS. However, accuracy failures have occurred, including McDonald's ending its IBM order-taking test in 2024.

With QR-code table ordering, diners browse, order and pay on their phones and the order goes straight to the kitchen and POS. Some restaurants have dropped servers for order-taking, but most keep staff in a hybrid model.
Vendors describe QR or app ordering as removing the server's job of bringing menus and taking orders. Staff are still needed at the table to deliver food and help guests.

Flipdish's AI phone agent takes orders and suggests specials, sides and drinks to callers, then sends confirmed orders to the POS. This shows AI can tell customers about specials over remote channels.
Pos Dish's QR and digital menus feature seasonal specials and new dishes, so table-side digital channels can carry the specials information instead of a server.
Dynamu AI, an 'AI waiter' for full-service dine-in restaurants reached by QR code, is still in early pilots. Spoken, in-person delivery at the table still mostly needs a human server.

Washoe County, Nevada licensing rules say a caregiver who counts toward the staff-to-child ratio must be physically in the room with the child, close enough to step in. Maine requires that all children can be seen or heard at all times and that sleeping children are checked in person every 30 minutes.

State licensing rules, such as Arizona's, set required staff-to-children ratios by age (1:5 for infants) that count only qualified human staff, and programs get cited when ratios or supervision fall short.
Childcare software such as Brightwheel handles side admin work: daily reports to parents, attendance and billing. The care itself is not done in software.

CDC guidance says sterilizing and sanitizing are hands-on jobs: washing bottles after every feeding, boiling or soaking items, or using a dishwasher's sanitize cycle, then air-drying them. A software-only agent can't do any of this.

Childcare standards (Caring for Our Children / Head Start) say caregivers must mix formula following the parent's or manufacturer's instructions and label bottles with the child's name and the date and time. All of these are physical steps done by staff, so AI could at most help look up guidance.
To prepare formula safely you have to boil water, mix by shaking or swirling, and refrigerate bottles and throw them out on time. Every step means handling the bottles directly.

AI activity planners such as Kidtivity Lab and Taskade's Children's Activity Planner can generate age-appropriate games, crafts and activity plans. That covers only the planning step, not running the activities.
Taskade offers a customizable agent that builds children's activity plans from a child's age, interests and learning style. A caregiver still has to carry out the plan.

Nanny work means caring for children in person and without supervision, which is why it needs vetting (for example a UK Enhanced DBS check). Running games, sports, walks and play dates needs a physically present, trusted caregiver.

The chore and reward apps I found (FamilyPoints, NeatKid and others) only let parents assign chores and track points or stars. A human still has to watch the child and give the praise; none of these apps does it on its own.

NeatKid includes positive-reinforcement features, but the praise is digital and gated by parents. Software can support the task (chore lists, tracking), while praising a child at the moment of the behavior requires a person who is physically present.

Nanny licensing rules differ by jurisdiction and usually cover the care setting and background checks. None of the sources I found requires a licensed human to assign chores or praise behavior, so legal accountability is not the main barrier.
Computer-vision produce recognition is sold for self-checkout (Toshiba ELERA, Diebold Nixdorf pilot at Aldi Süd). It identifies the item, but a person still has to put the produce on the scale.
Vision systems recognize produce and price it from the measured weight. The price calculation is already automated by the scale and POS system, so AI adds very little to it.
Checkout scales used for direct sale to consumers must be NTEP-approved and legal for trade. This rule covers the device, not a requirement for a human operator.

Cash-recycler and smart-safe software tracks cash and coin levels in real time for each till and clerk, and alerts managers when levels need attention. This automates the cash-monitoring step, but someone still has to carry cash to the till.
Avivatech's XpressControl dashboard shows cash on hand by cashier, till and location, and automatically alerts users to issues that need fixing.

Computer-vision queue systems count customers at checkout lanes and alert managers to open lanes when lines pass a set limit. This automates spotting staffing gaps, but a person still has to staff the lane. These claims come from vendors and have not been independently checked.

Benevity says its certified Workday integration automates payroll giving and cuts internal admin work. Third-party listings say it handles payroll-deduction donations and automatic corporate matching.
In January 2026 ADP launched Assist Agents that plan and act across HR and payroll workflows, with humans keeping oversight.
QuickBooks' Payroll Agent drafts pay runs and journal entries for wages, taxes and benefits for a human to approve. It does not run payroll by itself.
Monitor ERP's Agent automatically sends regular reports, such as order inflow and sales statistics, to the right employees in Excel or PDF format.
The OutSystems Sales Reporting Agent answers sales questions in plain language using the Customer, Order, Product and Supplier data stored in OutSystems.
The Infosys order management app on SAP uses agentic AI to give insights on order status, fulfillment performance, exceptions and reconciliation.

Motorola Solutions' Assist AI for 911 (expanded June 2026) streams live 911 audio, call summaries and transcripts to field units through CAD and mobile apps, and adds real-time translation. This automates passing information from callers to responders, but dispatchers still run it.

AI call takers handle non-emergency calls in Minnesota PSAPs. In Dakota County, AI redirected about 33% of calls in 2025. Emergency radio traffic and inter-agency relay are still done by human telecommunicators.

Some states require each PSAP calltaker or dispatcher position to be staffed by a person who has completed approved telecommunicator training (e.g., New Jersey, Florida, North Carolina). That implies a human must perform the work, though there is no single national standard.

A FEMA posting for a mobile communications vehicle job lists movement planning, operating and maintaining the vehicle, pre-trip inspections, and setting up and maintaining communications equipment. It asks for the ability to safely operate large commercial-size vehicles under federal and state rules. This is hands-on physical work, and only the planning, record-keeping and IT troubleshooting can be done in software.
A county telecommunicator posting says some duties are done outdoors in a communications trailer, so the worker has to be there in person.

Canadian Job Bank descriptions of emergency communications officers include operating radio and telecommunication equipment and coordinating vehicles and personnel. These are tasks done at a console, which software can help with but not physically carry out.

Canva Magic Design creates layout options from a text prompt or an uploaded image. A 2026 update reportedly lets its AI resize, recolor and adjust layouts on its own, so agents can draft sample layouts from start to finish. A person still reviews the result for brand fit and typography.
Canva Magic Layers (March 2026) turns flat designs into editable layered layouts, which supports automated layout revision.
Desktop publishing operators are not a regulated occupation in Canada, and no professional licence is needed to prepare layouts. The work is done entirely in software, with no physical step.

Flooring estimating software such as Measure Square can automatically create carpet cut sheets. It optimizes seam placement, layout direction, waste, roll width and pattern-repeat allowances, so the planning that follows the floor sketch can be done digitally.
Users still adjust the software's cuts by hand, and reviewers say moving cuts is clunky and some calculations are unreliable. A human has to check the plan before carpet is cut.

The main work is physical: rolling out the carpet, measuring and marking it on site, and cutting it with a carpet knife. An agent with no body or robotics cannot do these steps, so it can only help with the cut plan. No licence or sign-off requirement applies to this step.
AI maintenance copilots search manuals, work-order history and procedures to give troubleshooting guidance to technicians. The technician still does the physical repair.
Vendor AI assistants are sold as technician aids, claiming faster issue resolution and shorter mean time to repair. They do not carry out repairs on their own.
Some states, such as Hawaii, require at least a maintenance electrician's licence for electrical maintenance work and a journey worker or master plumber licence for plumbing work.

In O*NET, Packers and Packagers, Hand (53-7064.00) is manual work. Related tasks include moving products and orders by hand and placing them on conveyors or loading docks. My search found no O*NET task with the exact wording 'transport packages to customers' vehicles', so the task was rated as given.

The task means physically carrying or wheeling packages to a customer's vehicle. The reference AI agents have no body or robotics, so they could at most help with small digital steps like order lookup or pickup notifications. Not checked by search; inferred from the task and the agent definition.

Vendor sources describe AI-moderated and synthetic-audience concept testing that can run many consumer interviews at once and finish in hours instead of weeks. These are marketing claims and have not been independently verified.
By 2026, agentic project-management tools such as ClickUp, Wrike, Notion and Linear handle triage, spec drafting, tracking and reporting, but they hand key decisions back to humans at defined points.
A 2026 systematic review found that AI agents can simulate project-manager roles for planning and progress tracking, while humans keep the final decisions.

Funeral homes usually notify the Social Security Administration (SSA) of the death and help with SSA and VA burial paperwork. Survivors must apply themselves for the $255 lump-sum payment and for monthly survivor benefits. The work is mostly finding out who is eligible and explaining the rules, which is document and information work an agent can do from the case details.

The VA cannot pay DIC, survivor pension or burial allowance until the death is recorded in its system, and families need the DD-214. These are clear, rule-based eligibility checks that an agent could build into a personalized benefits summary.

Funeral software already offers aftercare and case-management modules, and some store burial claims and Social Security forms. The talk itself usually happens face to face with grieving families during the arrangement conference, so a person still delivers the information and checks it.

Commercial survey software (Carlson Survey, MicroSurvey CAD, Geo-plus VisionCogo) already handles COGO, traverse and least-squares adjustment, and lot closure checks. Leica Cyclone II TOPO and VisionLidar find ground points and classify point clouds automatically. An agent that can operate these tools could do most of the number-crunching.

An industry article says AI handles numeric data well but struggles with historical, vague or contradictory boundary descriptions, and that automated output must be checked against known benchmarks. That means a human still has to review the work, especially for property lines.
In states such as Oregon, Maryland and Oklahoma, surveying documents have to be signed and sealed by a licensed surveyor who is in responsible charge of the work.

SLB says its AI-enabled digital tools automated workover candidate screening and ranking at PGN Saka. It reports an 89% cut in selection time, with review moving from yearly to weekly across 196 completions. These figures come from the vendor.
A commercial AI tool is marketed as ranking every well in a portfolio by expected intervention ROI. This is vendor marketing, not independent evidence of performance.

In these BLM sundry examples, workover and plugging work needs prior regulator approval of a sundry notice that the operator's representative signs. The search found no rule requiring a PE stamp on a workover program, though the sources are scattered office-level examples rather than a statewide rule. In practice, operators keep an engineer accountable for the final rework design and spending.
O*NET lists fitting orthopedic braces, prostheses and supportive devices as a task for physical therapist aides, who work under close supervision of a PT or PTA and do only delegated, routine tasks.
An Illinois state position description requires aides to work under direct supervision of a PT or PTA. This shows the work is supervised, hands-on clinical care.

Phone-based 3D scanning apps such as SnugFit, Thuasne3D and SpinalTech3D take body scans for designing custom orthoses. A human still holds the device, and none of the apps do the physical fitting or adjust the fit on the patient.
O*NET lists packing body orifices with cotton soaked in embalming fluid as a hands-on embalmer task done directly on the body.
In Wisconsin, only a licensed, registered embalmer may embalm a body, and only in approved places such as licensed funeral establishments or hospitals.
Hawaii's rules let an apprentice embalm only in the presence of, and under the direction of, a licensed embalmer.
In Louisiana, funeral homes enter death records in the LEERS online system and can get and print burial transit permits there at any hour. This is browser work an agent could do.

In Massachusetts' default opt-out setup, a local burial agent must review the record and assign permit information before the permit can be printed. That means a human checkpoint outside the agent's control.

Passare's funeral software connects directly to Pennsylvania's death registration system through an API. Software already handles the filing step, but a credentialed funeral director still has to sign the record.

AI masonry takeoff tools (e.g., Civils.ai, Oncenter Takeoff Boost) measure block/brick wall runs, deduct openings and count units directly from PDF drawings; vendor claims cut takeoff time by up to 95%.

A 2026 independent study of Togal AI on a live commercial project found near-perfect count accuracy but consistent underestimation of area quantities, especially on exterior finishes, and concluded that estimator oversight remains essential.
Togal's own help documentation recommends treating automated takeoff results as a starting point to review before finalizing.

O*NET lists this as a core hands-on task for Helpers--Electricians (47-3013.00): operating cutting torches and welding equipment on conduit and metal components. The occupation is described as using, supplying or holding materials and tools.

Related task entries are also manual conduit work: threading conduit ends, connecting couplings, making support brackets with hand tools, and measuring, cutting and bending wire and conduit. A software-only agent with no body cannot do any of this. At most it could look up weld settings or read drawings, which is a small share of the time.
Plumber helpers cut and thread pipe with pipe cutters, cutting torches and threading machines, and help lift and position objects on site.
A posting requires helpers to carry up to 75 lbs and lift up to 100 lbs, mostly while standing or walking.
Canadian guidance lists manual material handling, bending and repetitive motion as the core physical demands of the helper job.

Robots that mark roads, such as Civ Robotics' CivDash, exist, but they are dedicated hardware run remotely from a safety truck. A software-only AI agent cannot do this work. It could only help with minor planning or record-keeping.

Most robots so far only do layout and pre-marking. Final thermoplastic marking, heated to about 400°F, still uses crews with truck-mounted or hand equipment. Systems like RoadPrintz still need an operator in the truck.

Under the MUTCD, pavement marking happens on site in work zones. The work has to be staged with temporary traffic control, and workers with traffic-control duties must be trained. All of this needs people physically present on the road.

Wisconsin DOT's maintenance manual says crews set snow-fence posts in the field before the ground freezes, then hang the fencing taut after it freezes, 35 times the fence height from the shoulder edge. This is hands-on fieldwork.
In a Utah DOT case study, a crew of three trained workers placed about 1,000 ft of fence in an 8-hour shift. The work is manual labour on site, and an agent without a body cannot do it.
MnDOT employees built a permanent 1,500-ft woven snow fence by hand after an agreement with the landowners. Only the planning and coordination around it is digital.

Manufacturing execution system (MES) recipe-management software stores recipe steps and parameter values, such as oven temperature settings, and flags when operators depart from them. This means pulling cook parameters from recipes and work orders can be done digitally.
Recipes are often stored on, or editable only through, the equipment controller on the plant floor. An agent may therefore not be able to reach those systems or paper work orders.

Under 21 CFR 113/114, thermal-processing operators must work under the supervision of a supervisor certified through the Better Process Control School, and scheduled processes must be set by a qualified person. Human oversight stays in place, but no one has to sign for the act of reading the recipe itself.

O*NET lists this as a core task for Cleaners of Vehicles and Equipment (53-7061.00). The work is done by hand: sweeping, shoveling or vacuuming debris and scrap into containers, then carrying the containers out of work areas. A software-only agent with no body cannot do any of it.

The occupation's other tasks use physical tools and materials such as water, cleaning agents, brushes, cloths, hoses and vacuums. This confirms the job requires being on site and handling things physically.
